## Context / Problem
The per-file comment-remediation tree under `lettered-depressing-willet` created excessive planning and coordination overhead. The audited requirements remain valid, but related files must be remediated together without losing file-specific constraints or behavior-bearing consumers.

## Approach
Use six subsystem workstreams and bounded directory cohorts. Each leaf owns a non-overlapping edit set, carries every migrated preserve requirement in its Scope, and records the same paths in file impact. Each leaf lands as its own Gerrit change on current `main`; the worktree is updated between tickets and immediately before each push. Leaves close only after both Gerrit votes are green and the change is merged. Stories and this epic close bottom-up after their children.

The replacement tree already supersedes the retired per-file tree one-to-one; the original epic and all 1,499 former children are closed as superseded.

## Migration inventory
Each story produces the sorted TSV inventory defined in its plan from live child, Scope, file-impact, and net-active `supersedes` state. At epic completion, the epic driver concatenates those six validated inventories, adds the story alias column, sorts by path, and appends the result to a dedicated `session_log` linked `relates_to` this epic.

Each epic row is `path<TAB>story-alias<TAB>replacement-leaf-alias<TAB>source-ticket-alias<TAB>scope-count<TAB>file-impact-count`. The epic completion comment cites the session-log id and records row count plus SHA-256 of the TSV. Passing requires 1,499 rows, 1,499 distinct audited paths, 1,499 distinct retired source tickets, exactly one live replacement leaf per source, `scope-count=1`, `file-impact-count=1`, and equal expected/Scope/file-impact path sets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every migrated file contains only current, non-obvious comment or docstring rationale and constraints after its leaf remediation; verified by the leaf row-by-row diff review.
- [ ] Every migrated preserve requirement remains explicit and accurate; verified by the leaf completion comment.
- [ ] Every behavior-bearing consumer contract remains explicit and accurate; verified by the leaf completion comment.
- [ ] Every audited path has exactly one epic inventory row; verified by the epic-linked TSV session log.
- [ ] Every inventory row has `scope-count=1`; verified by the epic-linked TSV session log.
- [ ] Every inventory row has `file-impact-count=1`; verified by the epic-linked TSV session log.
- [ ] Every retired per-file ticket has exactly one live replacement with a net-active `replacement -supersedes-> old` link; verified by the epic-linked TSV session log.
- [ ] Every replacement leaf passes `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, and has no unresolved comments before Gerrit Submit; verified from its change record.
- [ ] Every replacement leaf is merged to `main` before it closes; verified from Gerrit, `origin/main`, and the completion gate.
- [ ] Each story closes only after all of its leaves close, and this epic closes only after all stories close; verified by tracker state.

## Child decomposition
- Production-source workstream: authored package, CLI, MCP, reconciler, and review-bot source.
- Core unit-test workstream: unit tests outside the reconciler subtree.
- Reconciler unit-test workstream: reconciler unit cases and fixtures.
- Other-test workstream: interface, script, integration, external, and end-to-end tests.
- Developer-tooling workstream: maintainer and analysis scripts.
- Delivery-infrastructure workstream: CI, Gerrit, deployment, and infrastructure configuration.

Each workstream delegates to disjoint leaf cohorts and applies every acceptance criterion to its own path set.
